lead_headline: Dispatch rewires its own delivery stack in a single day, then reads the results aloud
lead_body: Fourteen commits moved the briefings pipeline to Vercel serverless, swapped TTS to Kokoro-82M via the Hugging Face Inference API, and resolved a cascade of ESM import and TypeScript errors that the new build target exposed. lead_article:
The biggest story today is Dispatch itself. Fourteen commits rewired the delivery stack from the ground up: the briefings pipeline migrated to Vercel serverless, TTS switched to Kokoro-82M via the Hugging Face Inference API, and a cascade of ESM import fixes — .js extensions, renamed api/_lib/ directories, TypeScript type errors — ironed out the rough edges of the new build target. The voice reading this is the first production output of that change. A local SQLite fallback landed in db.ts as well, which means the pipeline degrades gracefully rather than going dark when the primary store is unreachable.

Astro shipped astro@6.3.8 and a companion wave of adapter and language-server patches. The Cloudflare adapter's vite plugin config resolution was being called redundantly across multiple sites, which is now collapsed to a single pass. A Vite dep-optimizer race condition that was surfacing a false React-not-found error in dev mode was fixed, as was an SSR route-cache warning that had been flooding production logs since 6.3.6. The language server closed a stack-overflow path triggered by project references containing non-TypeScript files. On the Claude Code tracker, the volume of opened issues is high but closures were selective — the pipe-buffer backpressure deadlock under MCP permission prompts closed, as did the sandbox environment leaking into child JVMs on Windows co-work sessions and the shell-snapshot base64 obfuscation concern. The remote-control input-drop regression from around May 25 remains open.
